Unlike other types of emulators of this kind, the proposed solution is not only a qualitative assessment of the performance of the quantum algorithms, but also a method of their effective implementation using existing technologies. The paper will present the solution of representation of the qubit, quantum gates implementation as well as the quantum interferometer for a system with two qubits. To illustrate the proposed solution, we will also present the method of implementing a search algorithm: determining the parity of a Boolean function.

articleTitle: Gas flow and heat transfer in reflow oven
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Soldering is very important technology to connect components and printed circuit boards together. Heat is transferred to soldering joint using flow of air or, generally, gas. Heat transfer is depending on more parameters, e.g. distance between product and nozzle field, strength of gas flow. It is very complex issue and not easy to measure. This paper describes some ideas, how to measure gas flow and heat transfer inside of an reflow oven.

articleTitle: Environmental Assessment of a New Developed Camera System for Automotive Application
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Embedding technology is an advanced electronic packaging method which allows assembling electronic components not only on the surface but also inside the volume of the printed circuit board material. The resulting higher packing density of assemblies leads to drastic miniaturisation of the package and reduces the expenditure on materials. This work compares the environmental performance of a conventional and a new developed rear camera system for automotive application. The life cycle assessment method is ReCiPe Midpoint (H), 2014, based on the ecoinvent 3.3 database. The considered characterisation categories are Climate change (CC), Human toxicity (HT), and Terrestrial ecotoxicity (TE). The new demonstrator camera shows in all characterisation categories a reduction of the environmental impact between 55 % and 60 % within the defined system boundaries, compared to the traditional multilayer PCB assembly, and a mass reduction of 31 %.

articleTitle: Innovative System for Development and Analysing Sensors Integrated in the Airframe to Determine Losses on High-Voltage Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this scientific paper is presented an innovative technical solution for the realization of an airborne sensor system and determination of the main characteristics of the airborne sensors in order to detect the effect of CORONA on the high voltage lines. With the purpose of monitoring the high voltage electrical network, the behavior of the sensed sensors that determines the losses must be known, and for both sensors (ultrasonic and electromagnetic radiation reception) we have determined in the experimental model, the relative sensitivity and response time. To determine the sensitivity parameters and the response time of these sensor models, a series of simulations in PSIM 6.0 were performed to demonstrate the functionality of the analysis system developed by the authors.

articleTitle: Thermal Diffusivity Investigations on Alumina Substrates using Laser Flash Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper describes a procedure to measure the thermal diffusivity and thus the thermal conductivity of alumina substrates for power electronics. While the laser flash analysis usually obtains precise results regarding the thermal diffusivity, the measurements could be inaccurate for thinner thicknesses of the specimens. This is due to the necessity of applying a coating before running the measurements of thermal diffusivity which subsequently has a significant impact on the results at smaller thicknesses. Therefore, the manufacturer of the used LFA 447 measurement device by Netzsch GmbH recommends using platinum or gold sputtering at thinner thicknesses instead of graphite spraying. The latter is the standard coating material for almost every application because of its excellent absorption and emission properties. The following describes a process to obtain the thermal diffusivity of alumina substrates still using a graphite coating for the measurement applied by graphite spray cans and thus saving costs compared to sputter systems. The measurement procedure utilizes a linear correlation between the thermal diffusivity of the alumina specimens and the graphite coating masses at room temperature that was discovered in the following investigations.

articleTitle: Investigation into the Characteristics of DC Nitrogen Plasma Used for Group III-N Semiconductor Thin-Film Growths
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The active atomic nitrogen (N) species required for group III-N semiconductor material growth may be provided by a pure N2 gas ignited through a hollow cathode DC plasma system. An advantage of using nitrogen plasma over other common nitrogen-containing compounds, such as ammonia, is the ability to efficiently produce N species at significantly lower temperatures. Through the analysis of collected spectroscopic and Langmuir probe data, the characteristics of a DC nitrogen plasma source were investigated at room temperature and at a N2 flow rate of 500 sccm. The effects of varying plasma parameters on GaN thin-film growths on sapphire substrates were also investigated.

articleTitle: Model-in-the-Loop for Determining the Speed and Position of a DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper aims to present an algorithm for position and speed control of a DC motor. This system for control of DC motors is designed to work in a closed loop system. The reason for this system comes due to necessity to test more rigorously such DC motor, because are widely used in control applications. In order to test the DC motors and to track the response of these devices, a mathematically characterized model has been developed in Simulink together with real-time Hardware-in-the-Loop system. The benefits of this system are not just for the functionality and reliability of the devices, but also for reduction in development cost. Another benefit is in early identification of design problems and the repeatability of the tests.

articleTitle: Modelling of DC/DC Boost Converter in Visual Programing Environments
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The boost converter are the most commonly used DC/DC converters, especially for automotive applications, power amplifier applications, adaptive control applications, battery power systems, consumer electronics and communication applications. This is because the battery charge requires high DC voltage to be fully charged. The main object of the research in the current paper is to examine the operation of the boost converter in visual programing environments like Matlab and LabVIEW A mathematical model of the converter and its parameters are presented. The simulation results states that Matlab/Simulink is a suitable platform for control and regulation of the simulation processes, in additional to its dominant role in conducting research tasks. Similarly, LabVIEW software provides the possibility to be used for application that requires test, measurement and control with rapid access to hardware and data insights.

articleTitle: Discretisation and Data Reduction Algorithm for FE Modelling of Complex Multilayer PCBs with Embedded Components
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: A simple procedure for model creation of complex multilayer PCBs is presented using a voxel approach. A data reduction algorithm for the high complexity 2D layered structures using selective coarsening is described and the performance demonstrated using the ANSYS simulation software.

articleTitle: Fast Control System and Algorithms for Stabilizing of Mobile Platforms
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Modern equipment such as surveillance/night vision cameras, land and marine microwave receivers, visible and infrared sensors mounted on mobile platforms, require stabilized platforms to achieve maximum of performance. On these systems action various types of unwanted vibrations and movements that affect the quality of the information acquisition, leading to disruption of communications, blurred images and many other effects that decrease the performance of the system and have strong negative impact on its functions. The system under the authors' research was developed to be implemented on a mobile platform, compensating the effects mentioned above with a closed-loop control based on special algorithms (which will constitute a patent proposal) that actively cancel these displacements and increase the performance of the platform to a better level than existing systems. The paper presents the principles of algorithms, the BLDC (Brushless DC) motor driver based on Hall encoders and the results obtained in comparison with other systems.

articleTitle: Resonant Power Converters used for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The intent of this paper is to present a study about resonant power converters that can be used in application where a wireless power transfer (WPT) is needed. On the other hand, this paper presents a mathematical analysis about a resonant power converter topology that can be used to obtain a solid WPT system. Starting from the principle of operational for this circuit a mathematical equations system was described and was used to design a simulator tool for the WPT system. The major advantage of this tool is represented by the possibility to represent in a graphical manner the characteristics waveforms for current and voltage across the circuit. Also, this tool is very useful in design of circuit because allows to adjust the components of the system according to the quality factor of the resonant circuit in order to obtain a maximum power transfer.

articleTitle: Creation of Cavities in High-temperature Ceramics
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This article focuses on the creation of cavities in high-temperature aluminum oxide 96% ceramics. Cavity creation can be divided into the pre-sintering and sintering process. This research focuses on the creation of a cavity in pre-sintering ceramics. The first option is to create a cavity using micro drilling. This method requires expensive machining tools because of the hardness of aluminum oxide. Another method is to insert the filler into the structure before sintering, which evaporates during sintering. This paper analyzed the possibility of creation cavities with carbon tape for LTCC vias and graphite rod. The last part of this paper is focused on x-ray inspection of this cavities.

articleTitle: Exploration of the Possibilities of Low Temperature Soldering Alloy LMPA at Selective Wave Soldering (SWS)
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The report provides the results of exploring the capabilities of low melting point alloy LMPA [1] with Selective Wave Soldering (SWS) [2], [3]. Typical of this study is that a comparison is made between the commonly used solder alloy SN 100 and the LMPA based on the requirements of the standards [4, 5] and the business. The test results of this new solder [6], [7], [8], [9], [10], [11] were checked and completed [I2]. The real comparative results are given in terms of quality, possibilities, efficiency and effectiveness. Various critical product applications have been investigated. The experiments were carried out using a modern machine for selective soldering on sophisticated products, which is a guarantee for correct and stable results. Conclusions have been made that allow this study to be used for solutions and improvements as well as for future development. The results of this study can be used as a basis for generating of design rules.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Audio Signal Transmission System Using Wavelength Division Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The idea of this paper is to utilize the advantages of the optical fibers over conventional wiring methods in order to construct a system for transmitting analog stereo audio signal. The main goal is to create a low-cost analog stereo audio transmitting system using one optical fiber, with sophisticated sound quality. The system was built for transmitting an analog audio signals over plastic optical fiber by applying multiplexing over wavelengths. This method enables the transmitting of two analog audio signals over a single optical fiber. As a result, the audio signal can be transmitted over long ranges and using only one transmitting medium. In comparison with coaxial wired analog audio systems, optical fiber wired analog audio system has better signal-to-noise ratio, better frequency response and wider bandwidth.

articleTitle: Soldering problems of large size SMD PET capacitors during vapour phase soldering process
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The reflow soldering process of large size SMD components - having a dimension over 5 mm - were always challenging for the microelectronics industry because of the higher risk of component displacement type soldering failures like tombstone formation or skewing. In this paper, the possibility of such soldering failures was investigated during vapour phase soldering by numerical simulations on large size (4036) SMD capacitors positioned on FR4 printed circuit board substrates. A 3D computational fluid dynamic model was used for this purpose. The aim was to calculate the onset differences in the melting of the solder alloy at the opposite leads of the component. Then from the time difference the possibility of the component displacement during the reflow soldering could be predicted. It was found that considerable time differences can form in the melting of the solder paste which can cause the component displacement. The time difference is defined by the position of the component on the substrate. Not recommended zones on substrate were defined to avoid the component displacement failure during the vapour phase soldering process.

articleTitle: Impedance Meter based on IQ Demodulators
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The paper is focused on using quadrature demodulators in a measurement system. Quadrature demodulators are widely used in radiofrequency and communication fields. By using those demodulators, the measurement system is able to detect and quantify phase shift between the voltage and the current that flows through an unknown impedance.

articleTitle: Hardware and Software Modules for Education in Electronics Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Education in electronics manufacturing area requires both theoretical and practical knowledge. Difficult access in real manufacturing process, due to manufacturing area hygiene requirements, limits ability for practical knowledge accumulation. This paper proposes one way to overcome this problem. In the paper is discussed the computer network architecture that includes Moodle server, LabView server and the software. Hardware implementation, which includes TV camera, data acquisition system and sensors is suggested.

articleTitle: ALD Grown Dielectrics for Cap on a Chip: Fabrication and Characterization
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is a strong method of fabrication of high-k dielectrics with excellent properties. We present the ALD grown high-k CMOS compatible dielectrics used for capacitors on a chip application. Several dielectric films based on Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> were grown on high-conductive silicon wafers and used as on-chip circular capacitors with diameter from 100 to 1500 µm. The effect of the interface between dielectric layers was examined in oxide stuck-based films deposited by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Performed material, structural and electrical analyses of deposited dielectrics confirmed their highly promising properties for application in new generation of 3D capacitors, semiconductor devices and energy storage element.

articleTitle: Design, Modelling and Simulation of a Fifth Order Low-Pass Gm-C Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The paper presents CMOS circuits for integrated analog filters at very high frequencies, based on transconductance integrators. The design of a higher order low-pass filter taking into account the types of approximations: Chebyshev and Butterworth, was made. The performances of the filters designed were demonstrated by implementing them using the biquads cascade synthesis method and the state variable synthesis method. Starting either from the low-pass normalized poles, when using the cascading synthesis method, either from passive low-pass prototype normalized, when using the state variable synthesis method. The design of the transconductance cell has been done both at the model level and with transistors. All circuits have been simulated in order to prove the correct operation when implemented in a modern CMOS fabrication technology. As a technical contribution, can be noted the implementation and dimensioning of the main circuits, such as the polarization circuit, the operational amplifiers, the transconductance amplifier with active degeneration, applying improvements to the structure presented, checking the performance parameters and comparing the results.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis and Design of Wideband Howland Current Pumps Using Monolithic Current-Feedback Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the stability analysis of wideband improved Howland currents pumps using monolithic current-feedback operational amplifiers (CFOAs). Based on the application of the Nyquist criterion the possibilities of CFOAs for stable operation in the current pumps at output current i<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> larger than 1 mA and upper cut-off frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3dB</sub> higher than 100 kHz are investigated. Formulas for closed loop gain T = β<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> A<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> of the system with positive and negative feedback at active and complex load are presented. The complex coefficients of the amplifier circuit A<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> and the positive feedback β<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> are determined by using equivalent circuits based on the high frequency CFOA model, taking into account the input impedances, one-pole transfer function, output impedance and parasitic board capacities. Mathematical formulas for the poles and zeros based on the obtained coefficients are derived. Moreover, using these formulas a design procedure of improved Howland currents pumps are proposed. Verification of the defined hypotheses and the proposed formulas is performed by testing of sample electronic circuits using discrete passive components and commercially available CFOA THS3091 with maximum output current ± 250 mA and unity-gain bandwidth ≈ 200 MHz.

articleTitle: MEMS Microhotplates for Chemical Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this paper, we design and develop low-power MEMS based microhotplates for chemiresistive gas sensors using computer modelling and microelectronic technologies, respectively. Two geometrical designs of supporting beams of suspended membranes were designed and simulated to evaluate displacement in the structure. Two different patterns of heating elements were designed, and the power consumption was calculated. Fabricated structures are studied and compared with the theoretical data obtained from simulations.

articleTitle: Viscosity of Silver Based Nano-Inks
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The paper deals with the analysis and viscosity measurements of five commonly available silver based nano-inks at different temperatures. The kind of solvent, dimension of nano-particles and temperature play a key role for the viscosity of nano-inks. For the controlling of the deposition process of nano-inks by inkjet printing technology, knowledge of the rheological properties of applied nano-inks are necessary. It is really difficult to preserve the stable temperature in the printing nozzle during the deposition process, for this reason the voltage signal which is controlling the piezo-elements in the nozzle has to be modified due to the viscosity changes. For this reason, this paper offers the practical results from the viscosity measurements, which were done by rheometer MCR 502 Anton Paar. Furthermore, the paper offers the comparative study of the viscosity measurements of different kind of silver based nano-inks. The twin gap method was applied due to achieving of high accuracy of measurements. As the preliminary results show, the viscosity of silver based nano-inks has the strong dependence on the temperature.

articleTitle: Endogenous Heating of Printed Circuit Boards by Means of Electromagnetic Induction on Suitable Susceptors
publicationTitle: 2018 41st International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this work, methods for the endogenous heating of printed circuit boards (PCBs) by means of inductive losses in built-in susceptors are presented. Taking into account the inductive requirements, various materials are discussed and investigated which can be used as susceptors. In addition, elementary test stands are to be constructed and characterized, at which exemplary soldering processes by means of inductive heating are carried out.
